newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian brewery Saku 8-mo profit falls.
newsitem.headline: Estonian brewery Saku 8-mo profit falls.

text.p: The operating profit of Estonia's largest brewer, Saku Brewery, fell to 30.49 million kroons ($2.5 million) in the first eight months of the year after 35 million kroons in the same period last year.
Pre-tax profit was 31.19 million kroons versus 34.9 million kroons, the brewery, quoted on the over-the-counter market of the Tallinn stock exchange, added in a statement.

The brewery is owned by the Baltic Beverage Holdings joint venture between Finland's Hartwall and Swedish Pripps Ringnes AB, itself owned by Norwegian food conglomerate Orkla and Swedish auto group Volvo.
Saku said the beer market contracted by nearly nine percent in the first eight months due to a very cold winter and unseasonably cold summer.
It said beer sales were 32 million litres in the first eight months, versus 35 million litres in the same period in 1995.
But Saku said its turnover in the eight months was up 16 percent to 237.4 million kroons as it said it captured more of the beer market.
The brewer said it had some 57 percent of the market compared with 53 percent in the first eight months of 1995.
Baltic Beverage also owns the leading brewers in Latvia and Lithuania.
